title: Casio’s Crystal G-Shock Is the Most Expensive Ever Made
gist: Casio's 'Blue Rose Project' launches three G-Shocks, led by the $80,000 MRG-D5000 (20 units), the first retail G-Shock with a case and bezel made entirely of sapphire. It shows Casio moving upmarket into luxury watch territory held by Richard Mille and Hublot. The screwless 'Multi-Guard' assembly is so demanding that only one person at Yamagata Casio can currently perform it.

insights.claim: Casio's Blue Rose Project includes the $80,000 MRG-D5000 (only 20 made), the $9,500 MRG-B5000SA-2 (limited to 500), and an $850 GMW-B5000SB-1A, from a brand that also sells watches for under $90.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Halo products stretch the brand's price ladder and test whether a mass brand can win luxury pricing power.
insights.quote: This is quite the flex from a company that also sells its watches for less than $90.

insights.claim: At $80,000 the sapphire G-Shock sits, somewhat implausibly, in the same price bracket as a Patek Philippe or a Porsche Macan, and it enters a sapphire-case niche already occupied by Richard Mille and Hublot.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Casio is a mass-market Japanese brand moving into Swiss ultra-luxury territory, though at token volumes.

insights.claim: The 2017 sapphire G-Shock concepts each took over a month to machine and failed G-Shock shock tests partly because they needed metal bracing; the new model uses a screwless 'Multi-Guard Structure', inspired by Japanese timber framing, that spreads impact across interlocking pieces.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: It took about eight years of R&D to turn a brittle material into a durable product, which sets Casio's engineering apart.

insights.claim: Assembling the sapphire outer case required entirely new jigs and fixtures and is so demanding that only one person at Yamagata Casio, the company's main factory, can currently do it.
insights.speaker: Jeremy White
insights.so_what: Relying on one artisan caps production, which supports scarcity pricing but means the design cannot scale.
insights.quote: a process apparently so demanding that only one person at Yamagata Casio (the primary “mother factory” for Casio) can currently perform it.
insights.locator: To make the sapphire case work
